papers.title_in_file: Data re-uploading with a single qudit
papers.what_it_is: Simulation and IBM hardware study of data re-uploading classifiers built on a single qudit.

assertions.value: The authors report that a single-qudit data re-uploading circuit learns highly non-linear classification boundaries such as on MNIST, and that performance depends strongly on how the qudit states representing labels align with the label structure in the data.
quotes: demonstrate that a quantum circuit operating on a single qudit is able to successfully learn highly non-linear decision boundaries of classification problems such as the MNIST digit recognition problem
We demonstrate that the performance strongly depends on the relation between the qudit states representing the labels and the structure of labels in the training data set.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results from one study, mostly simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The label-alignment bias is a property of the chosen ladder encoding, so the qudit gain is data-structure dependent.

assertions.value: The authors report that without the squeezing operation the median accuracy saturates at around 0.7, while with squeezing it reaches 0.95 and higher, on the seven-class stripe problem.
quotes: Without squeezing, the median accuracy saturates at around 0.7 while with squeezing the median accuracy reaches 0.95 and higher.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study numerical result on a synthetic problem.

assertions.value: The authors report that when re-trained and evaluated on actual IBM hardware, performance is comparable to simulation only for the first two layers, then saturates and decreases strongly, which they attribute to noise in the entangling gates implementing squeezing. They state that only single-qudit circuits were investigated and multi-qudit circuits are a necessary next step.
quotes: when re-trained and evaluated on actual hardware the performance is only comparable for the first two layers, after that it saturates and then decreases strongly.
A necessary next step is to investigate the performance of multi-qudit circuits, since here we only investigated single-qudit circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limits.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum algorithms for scientific computing (Review Article, arXiv v5, 2025)
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2312.14904v5 (24 Sep 2025), titled Quantum algorithms for scientific computing; file name carries the earlier title Quantum algorithms for scientific applications.
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, sections 5 (clock speed and data encoding) and 6 (outlook); body of sections 2 to 4 skimmed by search only
papers.what_it_is: Review of quantum algorithms for HPC and scientific computing, with chemistry and fluid dynamics examples.

assertions.value: The authors state that potential challenges include encoding and decoding classical data for quantum devices and mismatched clock speeds between classical and quantum processors.
quotes: Potential challenges include encoding and decoding classical data for quantum devices, and mismatched clock speeds between classical and quantum processors.
assertions.certainty_reason: The review's statement of its own scope and the challenges it covers.

assertions.value: The authors state that clock speed mismatches between classical and quantum hardware can be up to six orders of magnitude depending on the hardware, and that good programming models for asynchronous computing on these timescales do not yet exist.
quotes: This is compounded by clock speed mismatches that, depending on the type of quantum hardware, can be up to six orders of magnitude.
we do not yet have good programming models for how to handle asynchronous computing on these timescales
assertions.certainty_reason: Review statement; the underlying figures come from cited hardware sources.

assertions.value: The authors state that standalone quantum hardware will support only niche applications and that interfacing with classical HPC is essential. They also report that companies forecast fully error corrected processors of hundreds or thousands of qubits by 2030.
quotes: However, standalone quantum hardware will support only niche applications.
Companies are forecasting fully error corrected quantum processors on the scale of hundreds or thousands of qubits by 2030
assertions.certainty_reason: Forecast attributed to companies; the review does not test it.
assertions.reader_inference: The 2030 date is a vendor forecast, not a result.

papers.title_in_file: Solving optimization problems with local light shift encoding on Rydberg quantum annealers
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, conclusions and outlook; results sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Numerical proposal for solving Max-Cut and MIS on a Rydberg annealer with local light shifts and optimal control.

assertions.value: The authors report that, using optimal control methods, their simulations obtain solutions for prototype graphs of varying size at time scales well within the system lifetime and with approximation ratios close to one.
quotes: Using optimal control methods, these solutions are obtained for prototype graphs with varying sizes at time scales well within the system lifetime and with approximation ratios close to one.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the setup is a many-body interacting Rydberg system with locally controllable light shifts mapping the graph problem onto the Ising spin model, and that the results come from numerical simulations.
quotes: Our setup consists of a many-body interacting Rydberg system where locally controllable light shifts are applied to individual qubits in order to map the graph problem onto the Ising spin model.
our numerical simulations implement the local-detuning protocol while globally driving the Rydberg annealer to the desired many-body ground state
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that the topology of the graphs is limited due to unwanted interactions, and that benchmarking against other classical algorithms is needed to learn more about performance.
quotes: However, the topology of the graphs is limited due to the issue of unwanted interactions.
benchmarking our method with other classical algorithms can shed more insights into the performance of our method
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limitation.

papers.title_in_file: Evaluation of Parameterized Quantum Circuits with Cross-Resonance Pulse-Driven Entanglers
papers.version_note: File name carries the arXiv v1 title Pulse-Level Optimization of Parameterized Quantum Circuits for ...; the file text (v3) is titled Evaluation of Parameterized Quantum Circuits with Cross-Resonance Pulse-Driven Entanglers. Same arXiv id 2211.00350, same paper.
papers.what_it_is: Pulse-level customized two-qubit entanglers for variational circuits, tested on IBM hardware for MaxCut and chemistry.

assertions.value: The authors report that customized pulse gates for ansatze reduce state preparation times by more than half, maintain expressibility relative to standard ansatze, and give PQCs that are more trainable under local cost function analysis.
quotes: Our analysis shows that utilizing customized pulse gates for ansatze reduces state preparation times by more than half, maintains expressibility relative to standard ansatze, and produces PQCs that are more trainable through local cost function analysis.
assertions.certainty_reason: Results from one study on IBM hardware and simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that their pulse-driven PQCs achieve a speedup of up to 2.9x with an average of 2.51x over a base PQC design.
quotes: achieve a speedup of up to 2.9x with an average of 2.51x over a base PQC design.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that the customized pulse PQC outperforms the base implementation in at least three cases, and that further testing with a more diverse set of PQC architectures is a next step.
quotes: Other next steps include designing a comprehensive entanglement model of the PQC by including spectator entanglements and further testing with a more diverse set of PQC architectures.
Our algorithm performance results show that in at least three cases, our customized pulse PQC configuration outperforms the base implementation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own scope and limits.

papers.title_in_file: Approximate complex amplitude encoding algorithm and its application to data classification problems
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, fraud detection demonstration, conclusion and discussion
papers.what_it_is: Variational algorithm to load complex-valued data into quantum states, applied to a compact Hadamard classifier on Iris and credit card fraud data.

assertions.value: The authors state they present a numerical experiment showing that the algorithm, applied to the compact Hadamard classifier, enables classification of the Iris dataset and credit card fraud detection.
quotes: we present a numerical experiment showing that it enables classification of the Iris dataset and credit card fraud detection.
assertions.certainty_reason: Small numerical demonstration from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the fraud demonstration is proof-of-concept: the feature vector dimension is N = 4 and the number of training data is M = 8, taken from a dataset of 284,807 transactions that includes 492 fraudulent ones.
quotes: for proof-of-concept testing, we take 4 normal transaction data
which means that the dimension of the feature vector and the number of training data are N = 4 and M = 8, respectively
The dataset has 284,807 transactions which include 492 fraudulent transactions.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup and scope.
assertions.reader_inference: Eight training records is far below the dataset size, so the demonstration does not test scale.

assertions.value: The authors report that the required circuit depth increases superlinearly with the number of qubits, implying that the method may not be applicable to large-size problems.
quotes: Figure 7 shows that the required depth of the variational quantum circuit increases superlinearly with respect to the number of qubits, implying that ACAE may be not applicable to large-size problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limitation backed by the authors' own simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the 5-qubit case, even when fidelity is reduced from 0.99+ to approximately 0.7, classification accuracy stays above 80%.
quotes: However, we found that, for the case of 5 qubits, even when the fidelity is decreased from 0.99+ to approximately 0.7 by reducing the number of training steps, the classification accuracy is still above 80%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single numerical result on the small fraud problem.

papers.title_in_file: A General Approach to Dropout in Quantum Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, conclusions, experimental setup text
papers.what_it_is: Defines quantum dropout strategies for quantum neural networks and tests them in numerical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that dropping parametrized operations improves generalization compared with no dropout and with entangling dropout.
quotes: In particular, our results highlight the importance of dropping parametrized operations, leading to improved generalization performance with respect to the case without dropout as well as to entangling dropout.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical results from one study on small synthetic tasks.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the working regime of moderate dropout probabilities quantum dropout does not reduce expressibility or entanglement, as the QNN remains highly overparametrized.
quotes: In this working regime, quantum dropout does not reduce expressibility nor entanglement, as the QNN is still highly overparametrized.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study numerical result.

assertions.value: The authors state that they run two regression tasks and one binary classification task, and that the classification set has 50 data samples split into 40% train and 60% test.
quotes: To assess the effectiveness of our approach, we conduct two regression tasks and one binary classification task.
for classification we have 50 data samples split into 40% train and 60% test
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Datasets are tiny and synthetic, which limits what the result shows.

assertions.value: The authors state that effectiveness on real quantum hardware and the theoretical generalization of quantum dropout remain for future work.
quotes: Future works may investigate the theoretical generalization of quantum dropout more in detail, as well as its effectiveness by running experiments on real quantum hardware.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limitation.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid actor-critic algorithm for quantum reinforcement learning at CERN beam lines
papers.what_it_is: Extends free energy-based reinforcement learning with quantum Boltzmann machines to continuous action spaces, tested on CERN beam line tasks with simulated and D-Wave annealing.

assertions.value: The authors state that the article confirms improved training efficiency of free energy-based RL compared with deep Q-learning on the TT24-T4 beam trajectory correction task, which has discrete actions and continuous states.
quotes: This article confirms the improved training efficiency of FERL compared to DQN on the example of the beam trajectory correction task in the TT24-T4 beam line
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one task.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid actor-critic with a QBM critic showed an increase in sample efficiency on the AWAKE problem, but a smaller improvement over the classical algorithm than in the discrete action case.
quotes: An increase in sample efficiency was again observed, but the improvement compared to the classical algorithm was not as significant as for the discrete action space problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one simulated task.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is not yet known whether the smaller gain is general or specific to the studied problem, which has linear dynamics.
quotes: Further studies will be carried out to test whether this is generally true or only for the problem studied here, which has linear dynamics.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limitation on generality.

papers.title_in_file: Software Supply Chain Vulnerabilities Detection in Source Code: Performance Comparison between Traditional and Quantum Machine Learning Algorithms
papers.what_it_is: Comparison of a quantum neural network run on a simulator and a classical neural network on the ClaMP software supply chain dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that execution time for the QNN is slower than for the NN at higher percentages of the dataset.
quotes: The demonstration result indicates that execution time for QNN is slower than NN with a higher percentage of datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single small study run on a simulator.

assertions.value: The authors report that accuracy, f1 score, precision and recall show a random pattern across dataset proportions for both the QNN and the classical model.
quotes: The accuracy, f1 score, precision, and recall results show that the quantum machine learning neural network model and the classical machine learning model does not have an impact on various portions of the dataset.
The results show a random pattern throughout the entire dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single study; the paper gives no significance test.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper shows no accuracy advantage for the QNN and gives no baseline beyond the NN.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QML model ran on an open-source simulator due to limited quantum computer availability, and that current simulators have a limited number of qubits that is not appropriate for software supply chain attacks.
quotes: Due to the limited availability of the quantum computer, the QML model was applied on an open-source Penny lane simulator.
the current version of quantum simulators comes with a limited number of qubits, which is not appropriate for software supply chain attacks
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limitation of the paper's own setup.
